implementerProof.how: Ran the implementer's commands again at 2f3bf214 on this pod's Postgres 17. The multiprocess package passed (669.1 s). The outbox (239.5 s; TestALaterEventReachesNoSessionTheFailedRecipientReadOfAnEarlierOneMissedBeforeIt, TestABrokenCreditListBacksOffItsEventAndHoldsOnlyItsOwnersLaterSessionCopies and TestAStoppingBatchReleasesTheEventsWhoseRecipientQueryFailed among them), deliveryaudit, duty, bus and cmd/listener packages all passed. I drove the review's two important findings on real processes myself, against the previous head as the negative control (proof below).

proof.criterion: Review finding 1: through a failed recipient read, a later event of the same issue reaches no session the failed read would have named before the failed event does (order per owner and destination)
proof.surface: two real envoy-dispatch binaries (multiprocess harness, throwaway probe TestProbeFailedRecipientRead) with a fake Envoy listener. Issue X, unrouted and unclaimed, has its spec created by session D; T1 wrote an anchored root comment and T2 replied. With both processes cut off NATS, a person's reply (X#4), a person's comment anchored on the spec (X#5) and a person's resolve of the root (X#6, which goes to the root's author T1) were written; the spec's credit list was set to a JSON scalar; then NATS was restored
proof.command: cd packages/envoy (scratch copy) && GOWORK=off DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<pg> go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -run TestProbeFailedRecipientRead -v ./cmd/dispatch
proof.observed: For 8 s while the read failed: T1 took nothing. X#4 and X#5 were backed off (attempts 4, publish_error 'load primary document authors: … cannot extract elements from a scalar'); X#6 was held (attempts 0) with only its owner topic reached. The watcher took X#4, X#5 and X#6 on the issue topic. After the repair (7.2 s), T1 took comment.created#4 and then comment.resolved#6; T2 took #4; D took #4 and #5. Every session's frames were in order
proof.negativeControl: The same probe at bf30591d (the previous head): nothing of the batch was published at all while the read failed (X#4-6 attempts 0, nothing reached); see the next entry

proof.criterion: Review finding 2: a broken document credit list backs off only the events that need it; the outbox goes on publishing everything else
proof.surface: the same probe: issue Y, routed to session R, got a comment written in the same window as X#4-6
proof.command: as above, reading R's and the watcher's frames for Y during the 8 s
proof.observed: At 2f3bf214, Y's comment reached R and the watcher while X's events waited
proof.negativeControl: At bf30591d the same window published nothing: R had only Y's earlier issue.updated, the watcher had nothing of Y, and X#4-6 were never tried, so the whole outbox stalled on the broken row until the repair. That is the defect the review found, and it is gone at the head
